subject: Clarify: default retention for requests vs responses (short digest)
messages:
From: James Lee <james.lee@brightbank.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.example>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example>
Cc: security@brightbank.com
Date: 2026-11-29T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Default retention for requests vs responses — quick clarifying questions

Hi Hannah / Kimberly,

Thanks for taking our questionnaire. A few quick clarifying items so we can map to our internal policy before the call:

1) "Requests" vs "responses" — when using Redwood hosted inference, what is retained by default and for how long? Specifically: streamed tokens during an interactive session (intermediate fragments) vs the final model answer.

2) If BrightBank chooses EU residency, will both request/response records and any derived artifacts (metadata, diagnostics, evals) remain only in EU regions?

3) If we trigger an erasure for a customer (subject access / right to be forgotten), what evidence can you provide that logs/objects were removed?

We attached our completed questionnaire as a starting point and would like a brief written summary we can include with our internal compliance ticket.

Appreciate a short digest (bullet style) and whether you need more info from our side.

Thanks,
James
James Lee
Lead Security Engineer — BrightBank
[james.lee@brightbank.com]

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.example>
To: James Lee <james.lee@brightbank.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>
Date: 2026-11-29T09:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Default retention for requests vs responses — quick clarifying questions

Hi James — thanks for the questions and the questionnaire. Short digest below; happy to expand or jump on a 30m call.

Summary (hosted API default behaviour):
- Requests (raw user inputs): transient by default and retained for 30 days. Purpose: debugging, abuse/abuse-detection, and quality regressions. After 30 days data is removed from hot stores; tombstone records retained for bookkeeping.
- Streamed tokens (intermediate fragments): treated as transient buffers and are discarded once the session finalizes; not written to durable logs unless the request completes and the final response is recorded.
- Final model responses (end-of-request outputs): kept for 90 days by default for quality monitoring and regression detection. These are the artifacts we reference in console traces and evals.
- Derivatives / metadata (traces, cost telemetry, anonymized usage metrics): retained 180 days by default; used for analytics and billing. These are aggregated and access-limited.
- KV cache / ephemeral session state: short TTL of 7 days in default hosted; cleared on session expiry.

Residency specifics:
- If you select EU residency for your account, primary storage and backups for requests/responses and derivatives will be confined to EU regions (no US egress for those artifacts). Some control-plane telemetry (non-identifying operational metrics) may still flow through our global control plane; we can provide a control-plane data map.

Erasure & evidence:
- Erasure request flow: we run a deletion job that removes objects from primary storage and triggers lifecycle deletions for backups.
- Evidence we can provide: S3 delete markers/tombstone IDs, job run ids and timestamps, and a deletion summary report showing affected object keys. For Hosted customers we can provide the deletion job output as a signed PDF.

Exceptions and custom retention:
- We can configure longer retention windows (for audit/regulatory reasons) on an account-specific basis. For Dedicated/Private deployments you control retention policy entirely; we provide the tools and runbooks.

Attachments: sending a short one-page summary (redwood-retention-summary.pdf) with the same bullets — see attached.

Next steps:
- If helpful, we can schedule a 30m call today at 10:30 PST or tomorrow morning to walk specifics and provide the deletion evidence template.

--
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Product Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-retention-summary.pdf (PDF)]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example>

Subject: Re: Default retention for requests vs responses — quick clarifying questions

James — quick technical clarifications to Hannah's note above: 

- Deletion mechanics: Hosted data is stored in object storage with index metadata in our catalog. The deletion job removes catalog references and issues object deletions; we then run a second job to sweep backups. We retain a short-lived "delete evidence" artifact that contains job IDs and affected keys which we sign and deliver.
- Proof format: deletion evidence includes timestamped job id, list of object keys (masked where needed), and a confirmation that the lifecycle policies were invoked. For regulated audits we can include S3 delete-marker logs and a signed deletion manifest.

A couple of operational caveats: 
- If a customer has long-term exported artifacts (e.g., snapshots they requested via export), those exports are outside of the hosted retention window and will not be removed by the deletion job unless expressly requested.
- For EU-residency customers we run deletion jobs within the EU boundary; cross-region artifacts (if any exist due to manual exports) must be flagged for removal explicitly.

If you want, Marissa and I can prepare the deletion-manifest template and a short sample of the signed PDF evidence for your compliance ticket.

-Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Director, Platform Security
Redwood Inference
